To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we synthesized short monodisperse pOPEs bearing laterally attached TTF units and found that these conjugates form mixed-valence complexes with a very unusual stability.
the TTF-pOpe conjugates are able to form multiple mixed-valence dyad complexes upon the first-step oxidation, and that these complexes are extremely stable towards the second-step oxidation.

short monodisperse pOPE units bearing laterally substituted TTF units have been synthesise by the Sonogashir cross-coupling reaction, that these TTF-poly(phenyleneethynyl) conjugates exhibit unusual electrochemistry, and that we propose that the unusual electrochemistry of these TTF-phenyleneethynylenes conjugates arises from the formation of stable mixed-valence complexes between the TTF and the TTF(+·).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of TTF-pO-PE conjugates and their electrochemical properties.
the synthesis and electrochemical oxidation of a series of TTF-pOFE conjugates, which form multiple mixed-valence species upon electrochemical oxidation.
the synthesis and characterisation of novel TTF-pOFE conjugates, and the study of their unusual redox behaviour.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TTF-pOpe conjugates are capable of exhibiting multiple mixed-valence states.
the oxidation of the TTF and pOPE moieties in these conjugates is strongly coupled and the resulting mixed-valence complexes are stable and persistent.
the oxidation of the mixed-valence complex of 1, 2, and 3 occurs only at the potential of the first oxidation step (0.49  V).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the TTF-pOFE conjugates are able to form mixed-valence complexes with unusual redox potentials, which are stable in solution and can be reversibly interconverted between different redox states by electrochemical oxidation.

the TTF-pOEP conjugates are able to form multiple mixed-valence states in which the TTF/TTF(+) units are separated by a distance of ca. 1.4 nm, which is comparable to that in the well-known mixed-valence complex, tetrathiafulvalene-tetracyanoquinodimethane (TTF-TCNQ).
these TTF-polymer conjugates can be oxidised to form multiple mixed-valence states with a remarkable stability.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the TTF-pOFE conjugates can be used to construct molecular wires with multiple mixed-valence dyad units that can be switched from the neutral to the oxidised states by electrochemical methods, which is of importance for the development of molecular electronics.
the TTF-pOEP conjugates 1-3 exhibit multiple mixed-valence states that can be tuned by changing the number of TTF units in a given oligomer.
the presence of multiple TTF units in pOPE oligomers can result in a significant stabilisation of mixed-valence complexes.
